findings.title: All four commits have no commit message body
findings.claim: Commits de164845, 0d91aa54, 7f48315d, and 617139df have no body, violating CONTRIBUTING.md's requirement that commit messages explain what changed and why; 7f48315d changes user-visible behavior (failed USE now discards the connection and surfaces a new ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError) with zero rationale, despite the PR checklist ticking 'commit messages explain what changes and why.'

findings.title: New tests don't call setup_tracing()
findings.claim: The new tests at connection_pool.rs:1474 and :1526 don't call setup_tracing(), even though CONTRIBUTING.md's tracing-in-tests standard says new tests should, and every other test in the module does.

findings.title: Fixes: #1682 references a nonexistent issue in this repo
findings.claim: The PR's `Fixes: #1682` points at an issue that exists only on scylladb/scylla-rust-driver; `gh issue view 1682` fails in this repo, so the annotation won't link or auto-close anything and should use a full cross-repo reference.

findings.title: Options/Startup proxy-rule forging logic duplicated three times
findings.claim: The Options/Startup proxy-rule forge is written out three times (make_rules at :1528-1568, and literal blocks at :1877-1889 and :1906-1930), all restating what start_simulated_node (:1809) already builds; should be extracted into one helper.

findings.title: decrement_total_connections loops N times instead of one atomic bulk op
findings.claim: decrement_total_connections(count) at :1360 loops dec_total_connections() N times; a dec_total_connections_by(n) on Metrics would be one atomic op and state intent more clearly.

findings.title: Hand-encoded RESULT/SET_KEYSPACE byte literal has no explanatory comment
findings.claim: Bytes::from_static(b"\0\0\0\x03\0\x08keyspace") at :1537 is a hand-encoded RESULT/SET_KEYSPACE body with no comment explaining what it represents.

findings.title: Test uses ShardInfo::new(...) instead of struct literal like sibling tests
findings.claim: At :1651 the test uses ShardInfo::new(...) where sibling tests use struct literals, an inconsistency in test style.

findings.title: Test matches proxy.finish() result instead of ignoring it like other tests
findings.claim: At :1689 the test matches proxy.finish() against DriverDisconnected where every other test does `let _ = proxy.finish().await`, an inconsistency in test style.

findings.title: Commit subject 'avoid busy-waiting' overstates a fix that still polls
findings.claim: Commit 617139df's subject claims to 'avoid busy-waiting' but replaces yield_now with a 1ms sleep poll loop at :1998-2004, which is still polling.

findings.title: Shard-aware-port keyspace failure has no immediate fallback retry
findings.claim: On error, the Connection branch retries immediately on the non-shard-aware port when requested_shard.is_some(), but the Keyspace branch just drops the connection and waits for backed-off refill; this is undocumented and asymmetric versus the spec's 'so the pool retries or drops the connection.'

findings.title: Unrelated metrics-balancing fix bundled into the keyspace-failure PR
findings.claim: decrement_total_connections changes at :674, :1031, :1114 plus three #[cfg(feature = "metrics")] tests and the unrequested_connection_event helper (:1854-2013), from commits de164845, 0d91aa54, 617139df, are not part of issue #1682 and aren't mentioned in the PR description or validation; should be its own PR.

findings.title: Keyspace check reordered ahead of maybe_reshard/block_advanced_shard_awareness beyond…
findings.claim: Moving the keyspace check ahead of maybe_reshard / block_advanced_shard_awareness at :913-928 is defensible (a failed USE no longer wipes the pool via reshard) and hinted at in the issue, but it's an ordering change beyond what was asked and deserves a commit-body explanation.

findings.title: USE failure log downgraded from warn! to debug! without being requested
findings.claim: The USE failure log level was downgraded from warn! to debug! at :903; with a non-empty pool, repeated USE failures now silently discard connections and grow backoff with no warning-level signal, though the issue only asked that the pool log the error, not that it be quieter.

findings.title: Checked metrics balance on new keyspace-failure error path for double-decrement
findings.claim: The report checked whether the new error path could double-decrement connection metrics: count_in_metrics increments once on open (:1051), the keyspace branch decrements once (:901), remove_connection only decrements when the pointer is found in conns/excess_connections (:1232), and the reshard decrement at :1114 runs before conns.clear() and isn't re-counted.

findings.title: Keyspace-change race can drop a connection despite the new keyspace succeeding
findings.claim: If current_keyspace changes while a USE is in flight and the stale USE fails, the connection is dropped even though the new keyspace might have succeeded; described as self-healing via refill and informational.

findings.title: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill test assertion doesn't prove a refill was scheduled
findings.claim: The test asserts need_filling() at :1509, but this is trivially true for an empty refiller regardless of the fix, so it doesn't actually prove a refill was scheduled by the new code path.

findings.title: Checked new ConnectionError variant placement and style against sibling variants
findings.claim: The report checked that ConnectionError is already #[non_exhaustive] and that the new variant's doc comment and #[error]/#[from] style match siblings at errors.rs:600-602, and found the placement sound.

findings.title: New metrics tests weren't run by the author before submission
findings.claim: The three new metrics tests only compile with --features metrics, which the PR's validation command did not enable, so the author never ran them, though the report confirms they do pass with the feature on.
